examples.text: In addition to the synchronous blocking I/O explored in the last two chapters, NIO also supports nonblocking I/O.

This feels about right, as does the idea that half a second will be taken up just doing disk I/O related to your page.
The final thrust of Bob's argument is that if you strip away all disk I/O (and he cites the move to SSD persistent storage), we'll shift away from interpreted languages such as Ruby and PHP and back to Java.
